title: Lanterns for the Long Crypt
story: The crypt beneath Ashenvault has gone dark, and Maelifrost the Chill Custodian herds shivering pilgrims deeper into the black. Mr 6 knows each lantern he lights pushes the dark back exactly 14 paces of corridor. The corridor to the exit stairs is 200 paces long.
question: If each lantern lights 14 paces and the corridor is 200 paces long, how many lanterns does Mr 6 need to light the whole way out?
hint: Divide 200 by 14 — then think about the leftover paces that still need light.
victory: Fourteen lanterns left a dark scrap of corridor, so Mr 6 lit a fifteenth; Maelifrost, who could only exist in gaps, had nowhere left to stand and politely evaporated.
imagePrompt: A long stone crypt corridor glowing with a chain of newly lit lanterns, a frost-pale custodian shrinking into the last shadow while a caped numeral-six knight strikes a match.
solution: Divide the corridor: 200 ÷ 14 = 14 with 4 paces left over.
Those leftover 4 paces still need light, so add one more lantern: 14 + 1 = 15.
praise: Dividing was the right instinct — the leftover 4 dark paces just needed one extra lantern.
